notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.45_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.45.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.45.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **Being in a call is always on screen, with its controls.** The bar at the
  foot of the column now shows whenever you are connected — which room, in
  which server — with a mute button beside the hang-up. It used to step aside
  whenever the room was visible on the server card, so the moment you clicked
  into a text channel the only mute button was somewhere up the list.

### Changed

- **A live channel's whole card is the way in.** Click anywhere on it to open
  the room; double-click anywhere to join. Only its name used to respond. The
  microphone button and "you are in" have gone from the card, now that the
  bar at the foot says both.

- **A channel remembers where you were reading.** Scroll up, go somewhere
  else, come back, and you are at the same message — older pages included —
  rather than back at the newest one every time. A channel you left at the
  bottom still opens at the bottom.

### Fixed

- **A call no longer ends because you are using another program.** After half
  an hour without anybody touching the Ruze window, the call was hung up and
  you were set Away — while you were playing a game with the call running, or
  listening with your microphone muted. It is now half an hour without anybody
  touching the computer, and on Windows that is what is checked. On Linux and
  Android, which cannot say, nobody is set Away or taken out of a call
  automatically at all.

- **People in a call no longer lose each other.** When two people joined a
  room at the same moment, the connection between them could end up kept at
  one end and closed at the other — after which one could not hear the other,
  dropped out of their room, and could not reconnect until somebody restarted
  the app.

- **Somebody who has left a room is shown as gone.** Several ways of leaving
  could leave a ghost behind: a "left" message dropped on a busy connection,
  quitting the app while in a call, a message that arrived after the one that
  followed it, and a slow sweep for people who had stopped answering. Each is
  closed, and somebody whose app has crashed now drops off the list within
  seconds of their presence expiring rather than up to half a minute after.

- **Leaving a live channel takes you back to a text channel.** When the room
  disappeared as you left it, you were left in a blank channel where every
  message failed with "that channel is not ready yet". You now land in the
  text channel you came from, or the first one there is.

- **A started live channel is called by its name in the call bar,** rather
  than "channel".
